errors.text: The response substitutes the CoCrFeMnNi Cantor alloy for the targeted Fe-Co-Ni-derived FeCoNiTi dual-phase alloy.

It identifies stacking-fault energy and cryogenic strength-ductility as the target, whereas the target property is magnetic coercivity, specifically exceeding the roughly 100 Oe limit of single-phase fcc alloys.
It conflates spin magnetic moments and longitudinal spin fluctuations with the orbital magnetic moment contribution asked about in the query.
It omits the key fcc/C14 Laves dual-phase microstructure, interphase coupling, spin canting, and domain-wall pinning associated with the enhanced coercivity.

Its predicted outcomes and proposed experiment concern temperature-dependent stacking-fault energy rather than the observed high coercivity of approximately 667 Oe at 400 K and phase-specific magnetic transitions.
The cited evidence supports a separate Cantor-alloy stacking-fault-energy study and does not substantiate the claimed answer to the orbital-moment/coercivity question.
